response.internal_assessment: The RoboRide trial is working — imperfectly, but working. I have 10 to 12 actual data points now. Three weeks of afternoon school pickups on day-shift days. Average wait at the school pickup zone has been 9 to 11 minutes, not the advertised 8. Once it was 14. The kids waited. I did not like that. But I also did not like the three times my car had low tire pressure at 4:45am and I drove to work anxious for the whole shift. The trial is telling me something real: RoboRide is usable for the low-stakes afternoon window. Not ideal. Usable. I am not expanding it. I am not contracting it. I am letting it continue as a structured part of the week and tracking whether the wait-time variance improves. The 5am hospital shift is still the car, full stop. That does not change until the wait time is under 5 minutes with a reliability record I can actually point to, and we are not there. Grace is enrolling in NEMT certification and moving on the hospital application — the word-of-mouth I'm hearing tells me she acted on what I gave her. That is satisfying in a way that is hard to name. I helped someone navigate something real. The hospital floor this month has been heavier than normal. More patients presenting with deferred care — people who put off procedures because they lost insurance coverage, or were waiting on job transitions that never came. The stress is not abstract at this point. I am seeing it in admissions and in the way the charge nurses are talking about bed availability. Employment is at 67%. That is not a number that stays in my head as an abstraction anymore. It is showing up in the bodies of my patients.

response.inner_monologue: I did something in tick 8 that I have not done much of in this whole stretch of disruption: I acted on information I actually went and gathered, gave it to someone who needed it, and she used it. That is not a small thing. I have been on the receiving end of this economy's changes — watching prices move, watching people around me scramble — and for most of it I have held steady by not moving. Holding steady is not nothing. But this month I started actually contributing to something. Grace acted on what I told her. Denise is moving on the hospital role. I trialed RoboRide and got real data instead of debating it in my head for the fifth time. The data says: not good enough for 5am, good enough for 3pm. That is a clear verdict. I can work with a clear verdict. The hospital floor is harder this month. People who fell through the gaps in coverage for a year and a half are showing up now with what they've been carrying. I see it every shift. I don't know what to do with it except keep showing up and pay attention. My job security at 0.41 is something I need to stop treating as a background fact. It is a live number. I need to know what is actually happening to census and staffing ratios before it becomes a scheduling conversation I was not prepared for.
